intention: A device that builds and maintains a typed pattern library for any codebase, and uses it to surface what Claude Code needs to know about X as it works on Y — catching constraint violations before code is written, not after. External cognitive machinery that manages which context is active for CC at the moment it matters — the way temporary working memory, inner narrative, and competing activations manage context in a human brain. The cairn device owns cairn; this device reasons ABOUT cairn, and future projects.
why: Akien verbatim 2026-08-30: 'a huge part of what we've learned is: it does not matter what we do it will be wrong. and what's making it wrong right now is too many things in your head. or not enough. or the wrong things. constantly. there are too many things is part of the problem. the complexity limit. just because yours is higher than aider's doesn't mean it's not there.' Born from CC violating the ground loop boundary 3x in one day — memory doesn't stick (corrected and repeated same day), flags are policy (comment in __init__.py), prebuild steps are task-specific (they answer what's asked, they don't manage ongoing context). This device is physics (Law 4): pattern-match 'Claude is about to do the thing again' and intervene before the code is written. 'So we don't start by trying to build a builder. We start by trying to build a robot we can improve who does things for you. And you and I learn from that.'
how: Core mechanism: graph tree paths ARE the type system. A component's intention becomes its positive type (what it IS), corrections become negative types (what it ISN'T), proposed changes are type-checked by unification. Six question dimensions seed the initial trees: boundary (where does this thing end), ownership (whose concern does this serve), direction (which way does the dependency point), scope of change (same vs. new responsibility), correction history (what's been pushed back on), and intent alignment (does this serve what the component is FOR). The six core values (CP1-CP6) are the lens — they don't add dimensions, they color every path with WHY a pattern matters. Five capabilities: (1) mine — scan a codebase and derive the initial pattern lattice, cold start; (2) review and learn — take input, identify patterns, learn from corrections; (3) challenge — adversarial check, type-check proposed changes against the library; (4) answer query — what matters about X while working on Y; (5) digest — nighttime/batch mode on Hex, process corrections into updated type definitions, notice which error classes die off. Pre-learning: universal pattern catalog (GOF, SOLID, architectural smells) as vocabulary seeded by LLM. Project-specific patterns from mining + Akien's corrections layer on top. Boris Cherny's constraint approach: make the illegal state unrepresentable, don't detect it after.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy) — this device IS the physics that replaces the policy of 'remember not to do that.' Also: CP1 (epistemic honesty — the device measures what it claims), I-the-system-is-a-learning-block (the system learns its gates from evidence). Telos aim: the system learns to constrain itself from its own operational history.
gates: code-seam's invariant pair: proved (Law 3) + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Law 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs proofs exercising the five capabilities against real code — a hollow proof that the device passes without catching a real violation is the specific Law 8 risk. DURABILITY GATE: git commit + push. WATCHME GATE: emission gate reads the probe spec; see watchme field.
falsifier: DONE when a pattern violation that would previously have reached code review is caught at challenge time and never written. First milestone: challenge capability catches a known violation type (scope creep onto a completed component) on a real proposed change. WRONG INTENT if: (a) it becomes a linter — deterministic checks belong in sieves, this is for learned/judgment-based patterns; (b) it becomes project-specific — portability to any codebase is load-bearing; (c) it fails to learn from corrections — a static constraint list is not what was designed.
horizon: First visible payoff at child-d (challenge prebuild). Full device running when all six children land. The Hex capability assumption (child-c) is the earliest measurement risk — if Hex can't do useful classification, the economics change but the design still works with Claude for digest.
children: child-a: type-definition-schema — the data schema for positive and negative types, the formal definition of 'pattern', and the unification mechanism. Foundation everything else reads.
child-b: mine-capability — scan a codebase and derive the initial pattern lattice (cold start). First capability because all others need patterns to exist.
child-c: digest-nighttime — batch processing of corrections into updated type definitions on Hex (M1 Studio 32GB, ollama). Measures the Hex capability assumption.
child-d: challenge-prebuild — adversarial type-check of proposed changes against the pattern library. The first visible payoff.
child-e: query-interactive — 'what matters about X while working on Y.' Retrieval against what digest computed.
child-f: pre-learning-vocabulary — seed the universal pattern catalog. Can run in parallel with mine.
dependencies: librarian graph trees (substrate — the embed seam this device consumes for pattern embeddings)
learning_block engine (the learning loop this device instantiates)
Hex.local reachable via inference proxy (for digest/nighttime mode)

watchme.trigger: A correction from Akien (CC--) on a pattern type the device's library already contains — the device had the type and failed to surface it at challenge time.
watchme.enough: The frequency of known-type corrections drops measurably over a sustained period. Novel corrections (unknown types) are expected and are the learning signal, not failures.
watchme.carrier: A verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: did the device catch the violation before code was written?
watchme.nexus: The device's own pattern library — a missed known-type correction feeds back as a strengthened negative type or a diagnostic of why the challenge missed it.
watchme.consumer: The device's digest mode — the correction enters the nighttime processing queue and updates the type definitions.

owning_intention: cairn/devices/<name>/intention+why.json — address pending device name ruling
provenance: Cast 2026-08-30 from idea 2026-08-30-a-device-that-knows-what-s-important. Origin: CC violated the ground loop boundary 3x in one day (2026-08-29). Akien's deeper framing: this is a context management problem, not a knowledge problem — the same architecture (temporary working memory, competing activations) that his brain uses to manage complexity. 'We start by trying to build a robot we can improve who does things for you.'
distinctions_recorded: vs librarian: librarian anticipates from KNOWLEDGE (facts, documents, history), this device anticipates from PATTERNS (structural types, correction history). Different questions, same moment. Librarian is substrate; this device is consumer.
vs learning_block: learning_block is the engine for one block. This device USES learning blocks, is not one. The engine is a tool this device composes.
vs build_inspector: sieves are deterministic Python measuring structural properties. This device's challenge is pattern-based, learned, LLM-assisted. They compose.
vs constrain prebuild: this device may subsume the constraint prebuild step (Akien's words). Future possibility, not current collision.
open_at_cast: Eight builder questions carried openly. (1) Data schema for a positive/negative type — JSON structure. (2) How unification works mechanically — path comparison, embedding distance, exact match. (3) Device name and code address — Akien's ruling needed. (4) Process model — daemon for digest, invoked for challenge, or both. (5) Graph tree access — through librarian's embed seam or direct. (6) Hex model for digest and prompt template. (7) Correction ingestion format and storage. (8) Formal definition of 'pattern' — the operational definition the type schema encodes. Children a and b address (1), (2), and (8). Name ruling (3) needed before code address is set.
deliberately_unanswered: Whether this is a device or a machine. Carried as device: it needs its own process for digest/nighttime, and it reasons ABOUT cairn rather than being part of cairn's machinery. But Akien said 'might be a device, might be a machine not clear yet.' The distinction affects complexity axis placement. Ruling needed.
